# Install

## Requirements

- [opencode](https://opencode.ai) 2 on your `PATH`.
- Node.js on your `PATH`. The installer scripts run on it. CI tests Node.js 22 and 24.
- Linux and macOS: `curl`, `tar`, and `sha256sum` or `shasum`.

## Install

On Linux and macOS:

**Install with sh**

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/belikh/OpenUltraCode/main/install.sh | sh
```

On Windows:

**Install with PowerShell**

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/belikh/OpenUltraCode/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

The installer ends with a summary of what it found on disk:

**Output**

```text
OpenUltraCode 2.1.0 installed
  Source:          /home/you/.local/share/open-ultracode
  Plugin entry:    /home/you/.local/share/open-ultracode/.opencode/plugins/open-ultracode
  OpenCode config: /home/you/.config/opencode/opencode.json
  Fusion panel A:  mistral/mistral-large-4 (variant max)
  Fusion panel B:  mistral/mistral-large-4 (variant max)
  Fusion arbiter:  mistral/mistral-large-4 (variant max)
  Commands:        /ultracode-debug /ultracode-fusion-models /ultracode-fusion /ultracode-research /ultracode-spec-audit /ultracode-verify /ultracode /ultrathink-fusion /ultrathink
  Agents:          10 installed in /home/you/.config/opencode/agents
```

Restart opencode after the install. opencode loads plugins, commands, skills and agents when it starts.

## What the installer does

1. It downloads the latest release archive and its `.sha256` file from GitHub.
2. It compares the archive with the checksum. If they differ, it stops and changes nothing.
3. It unpacks the release to `~/.local/share/open-ultracode`.
4. It asks which model each fusion role uses. In a terminal it shows a menu. Without a terminal, or with `--non-interactive`, it keeps the models of your earlier install. On a first install it uses the release defaults.
5. It copies the skill, the commands and the agents into `~/.config/opencode/`.
6. It adds one plugin entry and one permission rule to `opencode.json`. It leaves every other setting as it is and writes a backup copy named `opencode.json.backup-openultracode-` with a timestamp.
7. It runs `opencode reload` and checks that opencode offers each fusion model.

If an install replaces a skill, command or agent file that you edited, it first saves your version under `~/.config/opencode/open-ultracode-backup/`.

## Fusion models

The fusion commands use three agents with their own models. The release sets all three to `mistral/mistral-large-4` with the `max` variant. To set other models at install time, pass them as flags:

**Install with chosen fusion models**

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/belikh/OpenUltraCode/main/install.sh | sh -s -- \
  --panel-a deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro --panel-b zai/glm-5.2 --decider moonshotai/kimi-k3
```

If opencode does not offer a model, the installer prints the problem and exits with status 1:

**Output**

```text
  FAIL ultracode-fusion-panel-a: provider openai is not available in the running opencode (openai/gpt-5)
OpenUltraCode: the runtime check found problems (see above). Fix them with --panel-a/--panel-b/--decider or /ultracode-fusion-models.
```

The files are installed at that point. Run the installer again with models that opencode offers, or follow [Choose fusion models](../guides/choose-fusion-models.md).

## Check the install

In opencode, run:

**In opencode**

```text
/ultracode-verify "Call open_ultracode_status and report the mode."
```

The reply names the mode `verify`. If opencode does not know the command, restart opencode.
